written:
**A new salon signs up and its page goes live on solen.ch on its own. Should you have to approve it first?**
- A. You approve every new salon before it appears publicly
- B. It goes live by itself once it has payouts, one photo and one service (what happens today)
- C. It goes live by itself, but you get an email and can pull it down
I'd pick A, because one fake or junk listing on solen.ch is a brand hit you cannot take back, and the approve screen already exists in your admin area.

**On the salon sign-up form, the contact email they type and the Google listing it quietly finds are both thrown away. Keep them?**
- A. Keep both, the contact email and the Google listing
- B. Keep the contact email only
- C. Keep neither, just use the address they signed in with
I'd pick A, because the Google listing is the only way to pull their existing Google reviews later, and a lost business email leaves you with a login address as your only way to reach them.

**In the search suggestions, a barbershop shows "ab CHF 15" for a beard trim even when you searched buzzcut. Should that price be the thing you searched for?**
- A. Show the searched treatment's price, and no price when nothing matches
- B. Keep the salon's overall cheapest, always written "ab CHF X"
- C. Show no price on those rows at all
I'd pick A, because a search price the booking screen then contradicts is a surprise at the last step, the most expensive place to lose someone.

**The small grey text above input boxes, and the little line above a section heading. Keep both looking exactly as they do today?**
- A. Keep both as they are
- B. Move the input label inside the box, floating up once you start typing
- C. Drop the small labels, ask a bigger black question above the box instead
I'd pick A, because you already locked that a field must not change when you tap it, and today's small size adds no new size to the screen.

**On the payment screen, should there be a box where someone types a discount code?**
- A. Always show a discount-code box
- B. No box for now, discounts stay something the salon arranges directly
- C. Show it only for salons that actually have a live code running
I'd pick C, because an always-empty box sends people off hunting for a code nobody has, while the money side is already built and idle.

**On a salon's page, should anyone signed in be able to leave a star rating, even if they never went?**
- A. Only after a real appointment or walk-in (how it works today)
- B. Anyone signed in can rate any salon, like Google Maps
- C. Anyone can rate, but only real visits get a "Verified visit" mark and count toward the score
I'd pick A, because with a short salon list one wave of fake stars poisons the exact number people book on.

**On a salon's page, should a service show its description straight away, or open when you tap it the way booking does?**
- A. Tap to open, same as booking
- B. Leave descriptions showing right away
- C. Tap to open on the salon page now, decide the owner dashboard and settings later
I'd pick C, because customers see the salon page and it should match booking; the other two screens are for salon staff and can wait.

**On the salon owner's dashboard, do you want a panel telling them what to fix ("your Tuesday afternoons are empty"), or just the numbers?**
- A. Build it now, including the engine that works out the advice
- B. Numbers only, no advice panel
- C. Park it until real salons have booking history to learn from
I'd pick C, because today it could only invent advice out of test data, which is the one thing we never ship.

**On the dashboard home, the revenue tile always shows this week. Add a week/month switch to it?**
- A. Leave it weekly, the full week/month/year breakdown stays one tap away
- B. Add a week/month switch to the home tile too
- C. Make the home tile show the month instead of the week
I'd pick A, because that switch already works on the revenue page, and a second one crowds the busiest screen.

MERGED
The two label questions became one: the form-label question (grey text above input boxes) and the section-eyebrow question (the little line above a big title) were the same fork in different words, both asking whether small label text keeps today's treatment, and both answered by keeping it. They now sit as one question with the three real options.
Nothing else merged. Sign-up fields and salon approval both happen at sign-up but are separate calls (what gets saved vs who checks it), and the search price, service descriptions and review rules each govern a different screen.
